## Why This Is Asked
Tests tenant-aware routing, config-driven behavior, and simple path rewriting in a single component. It avoids hard-coded mappings and shows how to validate end-to-end with minimal manifests.

## Key Concepts
- Per-namespace ConfigMap-driven versioning
- Sidecar-based request rewriting
- Tenant isolation via X-TENANT-ID or namespace scoping
- Fallback handling and backward compatibility

## Code Example
```javascript
// Simplified path rewrite (pseudo)
const tenant = req.headers['x-tenant-id'];
const version = loadVersionForNamespace(tenant) || 'v1';
const rewritten = req.url.startsWith('/') ? `/${version}${req.url}` : `/${version}/${req.url}`;
proxyRequest.path = rewritten;
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test fallback to v1 for unsupported versions?
- How would you extend to support multiple gateways per tenant with canary versions?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to architect cross-cluster, tenant-isolated config rollouts with dynamic proxy configuration.

## Key Concepts
- Envoy xDS dynamic configuration and Aggregated Discovery Service (ADS)
- Kubernetes CRD-based policy model per tenant with isolation
- Canary traffic shaping with weight and time-based rollout window
- Multi-cluster consistency and safe rollback mechanisms
- Observability hooks for validation during rollout phases

## Code Example
```yaml
# (a) Tenant Routing Policy with Canary Weight and Rollout Window
apiVersion: cnf.example/v1
kind: TenantRoutePolicy
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-api-v2
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  tenant: tenant-a
  targetCluster: cluster-west
  route:
    path: /api/v2
    backendRefs:
      - name: gateway-service
        port: 8080
  canary:
    weight: 0  # Start at 0%
    rolloutDuration: 30m
    stepWeight: 10  # Increment by 10% each step
    stepInterval: 5m
  rollback:
    enabled: true
    failureThreshold: 5  # Rollback if 5 consecutive errors exceed threshold
    errorRateThreshold: 0.05  # 5% error rate triggers rollback
  healthCheck:
    endpoint: /healthz
    interval: 30s
    timeout: 10s
---
# (b) Sidecar Config to Watch Policy and Push Updates
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: envoy-gateway-sidecar
  namespace: gateway-system
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: xds-controller
          image: cnf/xds-controller:latest
          args:
            - --policy-namespace=tenant-a
            - --xds-address=$(POD_IP):18000
            - --sync-interval=10s
          env:
            - name: POD_IP
              valueFrom:
                fieldRef:
                  fieldPath: status.podIP
          volumeMounts:
            - name: policy-config
              mountPath: /etc/policy
              readOnly: true
        - name: envoy
          image: envoyproxy/envoy:latest
          args:
            - --config-path /etc/envoy/envoy.yaml
            - --service-cluster gateway
          volumeMounts:
            - name: envoy-config
              mountPath: /etc/envoy
      volumes:
        - name: policy-config
          configMap:
            name: tenant-policies
        - name: envoy-config
          emptyDir: {}
---
# (c) One-Namespace Test Manifest for Canary Rollout and Rollback
apiVersion: cnf.example/v1
kind: CanaryRolloutTest
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-canary-test
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  policyRef:
    name: tenant-a-api-v2
  testStages:
    - stage: baseline
      duration: 5m
      expectedWeight: 0
      checks:
        - type: metrics
          metric: requests_total{path="/api/v2"}
          condition: equals 0
    - stage: canary_10pct
      duration: 10m
      expectedWeight: 10
      checks:
        - type: http
          url: http://gateway.tenanta.svc/health
          expectSuccessRate: 0.95
        - type: metrics
          metric: envoy_cluster_upstream_rq_xx{cluster="backend-v2"}
          condition: exists
    - stage: canary_50pct
      duration: 10m
      expectedWeight: 50
      checks:
        - type: http
          url: http://gateway.tenanta.svc/api/v2/users
          expectSuccessRate: 0.99
    - stage: full_rollout
      duration: 5m
      expectedWeight: 100
      checks:
        - type: http
          url: http://gateway.tenanta.svc/api/v2/**
          expectSuccessRate: 0.999
  rollbackTest:
    enabled: true
    triggerFailureAt: canary_50pct
    expectedBehavior: weight_reverts_to_0_within_2m
```

## Why This Is Asked
This question assesses the ability to design per-tenant feature flag canary deployments in Cloud-Native Functions (CNFs), including CRD-driven configuration, deterministic traffic steering, rollback mechanisms, and observability considerations.

## Key Concepts
- Per-tenant feature flags via custom Kubernetes CRD
- Deterministic routing using HMAC hashing for consistent tenant-to-canary assignment
- Canary rollout semantics with percentage-based traffic splitting
- Rollback strategies and observability per tenant

## Solution Overview
The solution uses a TenantFlags CRD to define per-tenant feature flag configurations. The sidecar gateway computes HMAC-SHA256(tenantID + flag) to derive a hash value between 0-99. If this value is less than the rolloutPct, traffic routes to canaryPath; otherwise, it uses baselinePath.

### TenantFlags CRD
```yaml
apiVersion: cnf.example/v1
kind: TenantFlags
metadata:
  name: tenant-flags
  namespace: cnf-gateway
spec:
  tenants:
    - tenantId: "tenant-001"
      flags:
        - name: "new-payment-api"
          canaryPath: "/api/v2/payments"
          baselinePath: "/api/v1/payments"
          rolloutPct: 15
        - name: "enhanced-search"
          canaryPath: "/search/v2"
          baselinePath: "/search/v1"
          rolloutPct: 10
```

### Example Tenant Configuration
```yaml
apiVersion: cnf.example/v1
kind: TenantFlags
metadata:
  name: acme-corp-flags
  namespace: cnf-gateway
spec:
  tenants:
    - tenantId: "acme-corp"
      flags:
        - name: "graphql-schema"
          canaryPath: "/graphql/v2"
          baselinePath: "/graphql/v1"
          rolloutPct: 25
```

### One-Namespace Validation Manifest
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: cnf-gateway
---
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: tenantflags.cnf.example
spec:
  group: cnf.example
  names:
    kind: TenantFlags
    plural: tenantflags
  scope: Namespaced
  versions:
    - name: v1
      served: true
      storage: true
      schema:
        openAPIV3Schema:
          type: object
          properties:
            spec:
              type: object
              properties:
                tenants:
                  type: array
                  items:
                    type: object
                    properties:
                      tenantId:
                        type: string
                      flags:
                        type: array
                        items:
                          type: object
                          properties:
                            name:
                              type: string
                            canaryPath:
                              type: string
                            baselinePath:
                              type: string
                            rolloutPct:
                              type: integer
                              minimum: 0
                              maximum: 100
```

## Rollback Considerations
- **Immediate Rollback**: Set rolloutPct to 0 to instantly redirect all traffic to baseline
- **CRD Removal**: Delete the flag from the TenantFlags spec to revert to baseline
- **Gradual Rollback**: Decrease rolloutPct incrementally (e.g., 25 → 15 → 5 → 0) for controlled recovery
- **Version History**: Maintain previous flag configurations in the CRD or external storage for audit purposes

## Observability Considerations
- **Metrics**: Emit per-tenant, per-flag metrics tracking canary vs baseline traffic ratios
- **Logging**: Include tenantID, flag name, and routing decision (canary/baseline) in access logs
- **Tracing**: Propagate tenant context through distributed traces to identify canary traffic patterns
- **Alerts**: Monitor error rates and latency differences between canary and baseline paths per tenant
- **Dashboards**: Visualize rollout progress and health metrics for each tenant's feature flags

Why This Is Asked

Tests practical design of a per-tenant feature flag system in a CNF gateway stack, focusing on CRD design, a lean central policy API, and a sidecar with token authentication and caching.

Key Concepts

- Kubernetes CRD for per-tenant feature flags
- Sidecar fetch with short lived token and 60s cache
- Default semantics and tenant isolation
- End-to-end test in a single namespace

Code Example

```yaml
# Minimal CRD example
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: featureflags.cnf.example.com
spec:
  group: cnf.example.com
  versions:
  - name: v1
    served: true
    storage: true
    schema:
      openAPIV3Schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          spec:
            type: object
            properties:
              perTenantFlags:
                type: object
              defaultEnabled:
                type: boolean
  scope: Namespaced
  names:
    plural: featureflags
    singular: featureflag
    kind: FeatureFlag
    shortNames:
    - ff
```

Follow-up Questions

- How would you handle policy changes during traffic and cache invalidation?
- How would you audit tenant flag usage and prevent leakage across tenants?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

This question probes practical runtime config at scale, emphasizing isolation, zero-downtime updates, auditability, and integration with existing gateway proxies.

## Key Concepts
- Runtime feature flags per tenant
- Streaming update mechanism with local caching
- RBAC, audit logging, and change-tracking
- Minimal manifest demonstrating flag toggling

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: cnf.example/v1
kind: FeatureFlag
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-flags
  namespace: cnf-tenant-a
spec:
  tenantID: tenant-a
  flags:
    enableBurst: true
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you rotate the feature-flag backend and ensure no traffic drop during failover?
- How would you correlate flag changes with traffic telemetry for troubleshooting?
